reviews.paper_summary: A measurement-protocol paper arguing that a multiple-choice score should be tested against the construct's best constant, input-blind predictor (the "floor") before arms are compared, rather than against nominal chance. Four components: (v1) an arm-independent best-constant floor with an intentionally asymmetric decision rule (failing disqualifies, passing certifies nothing); (2) a balanced-null calibration of the floor estimator itself, since f_hat = max_L m_hat_L is upward biased even under uniform labels — this kills 5 of the paper's own 8 letter constructs (p=0.14-0.85), leaving only MMLU-Pro, MMLU, BoolQ at p<1e-5; (3) four under-specifications of the content-side longest-option floor (tie convention, length unit, tokenizer, meaning of "chance" when n_opt varies 3-10); (4) v2, an n_opt-stratified permutation null, explicitly disclaimed as the numerator of Cohen's kappa, with only the within-stratum stratification and the pre-comparison-gate use claimed. Evidence: 15 designated damaged cells across four model families on MMLU-Pro (n=12032) plus five smaller benchmarks with a mandatory power table; a single-cell fp32-vs-bf16 falsification of a numerical-tie mechanism; a 27-cell v2 re-judgement; and a 16-row retraction ledger.
reviews.strongest_verified_contribution: The winner's-curse calibration of the floor estimator, and the authors' willingness to let it demolish five of their own eight constructs. I re-derived the arithmetic: floors are exact label counts (1403/12032 = 0.116606; 3776/14042 = 0.268908; 2033/3270 = 0.621713), gaps equal 100(Floor - Chance) to the printed digits, and the partition into "above balanced null" (p<1e-5) vs "inside estimator noise" (p=0.140-0.853) is stated consistently in the abstract, intro bullet, Table 2 and Table 10 — including the concession that on CommonsenseQA and PIQA the observed floor is BELOW E[f_hat]. Also verified: the 36-item stratification gap (Sum_s w_s max_L m_{s,L} = 1439/12032 vs f_const = 1403/12032, exactly 0.2992 pp), with the paper correctly refusing to call the v1 >= v2 ordering a theorem and exhibiting the n_opt-conditional emitter that attains f_const + 0.299 pp; and the binomial back-stop P(X>=3 | 12, 0.05) = 0.019568, matching the quoted 0.0196.
strengths: Quantifies the bias of its own headline estimator and then retracts the quantitative form of its own claim on 5 of 8 constructs. Verified consistent across abstract, intro, Table 2 (tab_nulls) and Table 10 (tab_construct_nulls), including the admission that CommonsenseQA and PIQA floors sit below E[f_hat].

Zero fabricated or mis-venued references across all 17 bib entries, verified with the correct authority per family. ACL family via Anthology: Balepur 2024.acl-long.555 pp.10308-10330; OLMES 2025.findings-naacl.282 pp.5020-5048 (Findings of NAACL 2025, matching the bib exactly, no CoRR fallback); Hewitt D19-1275 pp.2733-2743; Feng P19-1554 pp.5533-5538. OpenReview family via venueid: Cho ICLR.cc/2026/Conference with a Camera_Ready_Revision invitation, Oostermeijer ICML.cc/2026/Conference, Zheng2025 ICLR.cc/2025/Conference (Oral), Zheng2024 ICLR.cc/2024/Conference (spotlight). Ding via DBLP: NeurIPS 2021 pp.1556-1568, Conference-and-Workshop type (not CoRR). Arcon correctly labelled arXiv preprint.

Load-bearing citation claims verified against source PDFs rather than assumed. I extracted all 27 checklist items across the 8 recommendations of Bean et al. (arXiv 2511.04703) and confirmed NONE asks for a null, chance level, or constant predictor — the intro's claim is precisely correct. Feng et al. P19-1554 Sec 3.1 does construct a dataset where a hypothesis-only baseline is capped at chance while artifacts stay exploitable. OLMES's camera-ready does take the better of MCF/CF per task-model and frames its reference around a random baseline, with no label-marginal floor anywhere. Balepur's footnote 4 does define the majority-class baseline as most-frequent-choice and Sec 2 does impute 0.25 for invalid outputs.

The v2 prior-art paragraph is written the right way: it names five kappa-family works, says 'we claim none of it', and then states one specific boundary (k varying item-to-item with the permutation confined within strata). All five verified via Crossref: Bennett 1954 POQ 18(3):303; Brennan & Prediger 1981 EPM 41(3):687-699; Frary 1988 EMIP 7(2):33-38; Brenner & Kliebsch 1996 Epidemiology 7(2):199-202; De Vries 2008 Field Methods 20(3):272-282; Cohen 1960 EPM 20(1):37-46.

Refuses to overclaim the v1 >= v2 ordering. States it as a measured property under an explicit, stated-not-assumed regularity condition; gives the tightest cell's attainable violation (0.085 pp); notes that 13 of 27 cells could not have violated the bound under any prediction vector so the 27-cell count overstates the evidence; and exhibits a legal n_opt-conditional emitter that beats f_const.

Multiplicity is handled by disclosure rather than by a convenient family definition. App A.5 states outright that under BH q=0.05 or Bonferroni NEITHER reference retains a single cell (0/12 both sides) and that the corrected comparison is undefined, then falls back to a defensible binomial statement on the count.

A 16-row flat retraction ledger with a machine-readable claim-evidence map, including 6 retracted and 2 prohibited numeric claims, and a named list of deprecated numbers not to resurrect. The regime confound (OLMo-2 prune-then-heal vs non-OLMo evaluation-time truncation) is labelled in Sec 4, in Table 5's caption, and in Limitations.

issues.location: Sec 2 Related Work (all four paragraphs); Sec 3.1 (read-out v1 definition); refs.bib
issues.description: The core method — compare accuracy to the largest-class rate and test the difference — is the No Information Rate, standard classification practice shipped in mainstream tooling since 2008, and the paper never engages that literature. caret::confusionMatrix documents: 'a one-sided test to see if the accuracy is better than the no information rate, which is taken to be the largest class percentage in the data' (verified against the package documentation; Kuhn 2008, Journal of Statistical Software 28(5), verified via Crossref 10.18637/jss.v028.i05). That is read-out v1 plus a significance test, applied by default to every confusion matrix. The Related Work cites Balepur, Zheng 2025, Zheng 2024, OLMES, Cho, Feng, Hewitt & Liang, Ding, Bean, and five kappa-family papers for v2 — a genuine effort — but never touches the classification-metrics literature where the arm-independent floor test already lives. The consequence is that 'the missing operational item' reads as newly invented, when the true and still-publishable statement is narrower: the item is missing from LLM benchmark reporting practice, not from measurement methodology.

State plainly that v1 IS the NIR test applied per-arm to likelihood-scored MC constructs, and relocate the paper's novelty to what survives: (a) the winner's-curse calibration of the floor estimator, (b) the four under-specifications of the content-side floor, (c) the n_opt-varying stratification for v2. Change 'Our contribution is to make the construct-appropriate input-blind null a pre-comparison gate' to a claim about adoption in LLM MC reporting, not about inventing the reference.

reviews.paper_summary: The paper proposes "null calibration" as a reporting protocol for multiple-choice LM evaluation: before comparing model arms, test the reported score against the construct's best constant, input-blind predictor (max gold-label marginal for letter constructs; a longest-option heuristic for content-likelihood constructs), treating the floor pass as necessary but not sufficient. Four contributions follow. (1) The floor is not nominal chance (BoolQ 0.6217 vs 0.50; MMLU-Pro 0.116606 vs 0.100000), and because the floor estimator is a maximum over k noisy label marginals it is itself upward biased; after calibration against a balanced null at each construct's own (n,k), only 3 of 8 letter constructs (MMLU-Pro, MMLU, BoolQ) have floors a balanced null could not produce, while five lie inside the estimator's own sampling noise. (2) Content floors are under-specified by four independent degrees of freedom: tie convention (0.125914 to 0.532164 on MMLU-Pro), length unit, tokenizer, and the meaning of "chance" when n_opt varies. (3) On MMLU-Pro (n=12032), 14 of 15 designated damaged cells across four model families sit at or below their floor while reading above a chance line; held to a symmetric bootstrap standard the flip is 3/12 vs 1/12, and under BH or Bonferroni neither side retains a cell. (4) A complementary arm-conditional permutation null (read-out v2, the numerator of Cohen's kappa stratified by n_opt) is exactly zero for any constant emitter and is used to re-judge 27 previously scored cells, withdrawing one above-floor capability label and dissolving two below-floor competence labels. A full-fp32 control removes all bf16 exact ties and changes 18.03% of letter decisions without recovering accuracy.
reviews.strongest_verified_contribution: The winner's-curse calibration of the best-constant floor, together with the authors' willingness to let it narrow their own headline from eight constructs to three. That f_hat = max_L m_hat_L is upward biased on a finite item set is obvious once stated and does not appear in the MC-baseline literature the paper positions against (balepur2024artifacts, gu2025olmes, zheng2024selectors). Table 1 operationalises it with E[f_hat], q_95 and p columns, and its caption does the honest thing: it states that only MMLU-Pro, MMLU and BoolQ survive (p<1e-5), that the other five are inside estimator noise (p=0.140-0.853), and that CommonsenseQA and PIQA floors are in fact BELOW E[f_hat]. I verified every Gap column equals 100*(Floor-Chance) to printed precision, and that the abstract carries this narrowing rather than hiding it. The 200,000-draw simulation itself I could not re-run (no evidence file shipped).
strengths: Unusual and verifiable scoping discipline: the paper does not append a caveat, it moves its own headline. Sec 5.1's "Both sides of the flip, held to one standard" voluntarily reduces the flip from 10/12-vs-1/12 to 3/12-vs-1/12 ("about a third of its advertised size") and then reports that under BH or Bonferroni NEITHER reference retains a cell. Table 1's caption states only 3 of 8 constructs survive calibration. Table 11 is a 16-row retraction ledger with six retracted and two prohibited claims.

The v1/v2 separation is genuinely clarifying and non-circular. The observation that an arm-independent best-constant floor cannot serve as a competence statistic (always-A / always-E / always-J score 0.000 / -2.111 / -3.807 pp on MMLU-Pro while carrying identical item-level information, i.e. none) is the sharpest idea in the paper and motivates v2 on its own terms.

Novelty boundaries drawn at the right size and stated precisely. Sec 3.2 states outright that Delta_perm IS the numerator of Cohen's kappa, that the constant-emitter zero is the textbook property, and that option-count-aware chance correction is decades old, citing five primary sources (Bennett 1954, Brennan & Prediger 1981, Frary 1988, Brenner & Kliebsch 1996, De Vries 2008) which I verified all resolve via Crossref with exactly the printed titles, authors, volumes, issues, pages and years. The claim reduces to varying-k stratification plus use as a pre-comparison gate.

The v1/v2 ordering is explicitly refused as an identity. Appendix A.3 gives the exact counterexample (an n_opt-conditional emitter A,A,B,E,B,E,A,A legal on every item attaining f_const + 0.299 pp), explains why "holds in 27/27 cells" overstates the evidence (13 cells could not have violated it under any prediction vector), reduces binding evidence to one cell's 0.085 pp attainable violation, and bolds "Passing v2 must never be described as clearing the paper's floor." I verified the 36-item / 0.299 pp slack arithmetic: (1439-1403)/12032 = 0.2992%.

Load-bearing citations are mostly accurate at the sentence level. I confirmed via arXiv 2602.02182 that the opening anecdote is real ("Although all models perform above chance, they fail to outperform the majority-class baseline"), and via the OLMES arXiv v2 full text that the max-of-MCF/CF rule and its random-baseline reference framing are correctly characterised in Sec 2.

reviews.paper_summary: A measurement-protocol paper arguing that a multiple-choice score must be tested against its construct's best input-blind predictor (v1: the best constant letter under the empirical gold marginal; a longest-option heuristic for content likelihood) before arms are compared, since "above chance" can credit an empty predictor. Four load-bearing claims: (H1) the floor is not chance and, for content, is under-specified by tie convention, length unit and tokenizer, with a fourth degree of freedom when option count varies; (H2) the floor estimator is itself upward biased as a max over k noisy marginals and must be calibrated, after which only MMLU-Pro, MMLU and BoolQ survive at p<1e-5 while five constructs fall inside estimator noise; (H3) the reference choice flips readings, with 14/15 designated damaged cells at or below the floor while reading above chance, shrinking to 3/12 vs 1/12 under one symmetric bootstrap standard; (H4) a within-n_opt-stratum arm-conditional permutation null (Cohen's kappa numerator), exactly zero for any constant emitter, re-sorts 27 previously scored cells. The paper ships a 16-row retraction ledger, a prohibited-numbers row, and discloses three integrity defects with measured impact.
reviews.strongest_verified_contribution: The internal arithmetic of the measurement tables is genuinely reproducible and I verified it end-to-end. All 27 rows of Table 7 (tab_v2_full) satisfy Delta_perm = 100*(acc - acc_hat) to printing precision (0/27 mismatches); all 11 MMLU-Pro cells in Table 4 satisfy Delta = 100*(acc - 0.116606) against the same always-A floor, and Table 4's accuracies agree with the independent Table 7 listing of those cells. Every one of the 8 floors in Table 1 is an exact integer label count over n (1403/12032, 3776/14042, 138/500, 633/2376, 311/1172, 255/1221, 928/1838, 2033/3270), which is what a genuine label-marginal floor must look like and is strong evidence they were computed from real per-item records rather than transcribed. Gaps and ratios reproduce in 9/9 Table 1 rows; the +38.76 pp ARC-Easy content-letter gap, the 18.03% fp32 flip rate (2532/14042), the 36-item / 0.299 pp stratification slack, the 0.0078 pp tightest margin, the 94.8% A-argmax weight (11409/12032), and the 0.0196 binomial P(X>=3|12,0.05) all reproduce exactly.
strengths: Table-level arithmetic is verifiably self-consistent: 0/27 mismatches in Table 7's Delta_perm, 0/11 in Table 4's floor deltas, and all 8 floors are exact integer label counts over n — I recomputed each independently.

Unusually disciplined self-falsification: a 16-row status ledger with 6 retracted and 2 prohibited numeric claims, a paragraph that voluntarily shrinks the paper's own headline from 10/12-vs-1/12 to 3/12-vs-1/12 under a symmetric standard, and an explicit statement that under BH/Bonferroni neither reference retains a single cell (0/12) so the corrected comparison is undefined.

Integrity defects are disclosed with measured impact rather than hidden: the illegal bootstrap p=1.042 (0/24 verdicts changed, 0/30 p-values crossed 0.05), the tokenizer-mismatched sequence cap that silently truncated 10/15 cells (0/14 verdicts, <=0.0083 pp, with the honest note that benignity was unknowable in advance), and the Llama-2 OOM that the merge guard correctly refused.

The v1/v2 ordering is correctly presented as a measured property under a stated regularity condition rather than a theorem, with the per-stratum argmax worked out (B,E,B,E for n_opt=5..8), the exact 36-item slack, the tightest cell's attainable violation (0.085 pp), and a concrete n_opt-conditional emitter that violates it — this is the right epistemic standard and I verified the arithmetic.

The constant-collapse identity for v2 is genuinely algebraic, prior art on option-count-aware chance correction is attributed claim by claim (Bennett, Brennan-Prediger, Frary, Brenner-Kliebsch, De Vries), and the paper explicitly disclaims the statistic itself, claiming only the varying-k stratification and gate use.

Citation local support is good where I could check it: arcon2026metalinguistic's abstract does state models are above chance yet fail to beat the majority-class baseline, and bean2025measuring genuinely contains zero occurrences of 'null', 'majority' or 'constant' as reference lines, supporting the paper's 'missing checklist item' framing. issues.description: The winner's-curse calibration — the paper's own methodological centrepiece — uses a null that is misspecified for MMLU-Pro, in the direction that flatters the claim. Table 10 prints k=10 for both MMLU-Pro rows and the caption states 'exactly balanced multinomial null at that construct's own (n,k)', i.e. gold drawn uniform over ten letters on every item. But the paper's own Appendix A.1.4 establishes that n_opt ranges from 3 to 10 and mean(1/n_opt)=0.110877, so letters are NOT equiprobable over the item set. There is a deterministic contradiction requiring no simulation: letter A is legal on every MMLU-Pro item, so under any item-wise-balanced null E[m_hat_A] = mean(1/n_opt) = 0.110877, and since f_hat = max_L m_hat_L >= m_hat_A we must have E[f_hat] >= 0.110877. Table 1's item-average row prints E[f_hat] = 0.104460, BELOW its own Chance column of 0.110877 — an upward-biased maximum cannot have expectation below one of the terms it maximises over. I reproduced the paper's recipe exactly (Multinomial(12032, uniform over 10), 2e5 draws: E=0.104463, q95=0.107048, p=0.0 vs printed 0.104457/0.107048/<1e-5), confirming the script does what the caption says and that the recipe itself is wrong. Simulating the correct item-wise-legal null over every n_opt histogram consistent with the paper's own three stated constraints (n_opt in 3..10; 623 items in strata 5-8; mean(1/n_opt)=0.110877) gives E[f_hat]=0.1135-0.1138, q95=0.1170-0.1174, and p(f_hat>=0.116606) = 0.064-0.087 across 8 admissible histograms — i.e. the observed floor lies INSIDE the correctly specified estimator's noise, not at p<1e-5. Note also sd(m_hat_A)=0.002862, so the floor is only 2.0 sd above E[m_hat_A] before the max is even taken. MMLU-Pro is the flagship construct (only MMLU-scale n; source of 14/15, of 3/12-vs-1/12, and of all 27 v2 cells), so under the correct null the abstract's 'three of eight' most likely becomes 'two of eight'. ARC-Easy (chance 0.250161) and ARC-Challenge (0.250156) also have non-round chance lines proving varying n_opt while their rows print k=4, so they are affected too, though their verdicts are already 'inside noise' and would not flip direction. This does NOT touch H1 for BoolQ (12.17 pp gap, no plausible null), nor H3 (ordinal comparisons against a fixed floor), nor H4.
issues.proposed_fix: Recompute the calibration under the construct's actual label-legality structure: draw each item's gold uniform over that item's legal letters (equivalently, per-stratum Multinomial(n_s, uniform over k_s) summed to a 10-letter marginal), then recompute E[f_hat], q95 and p. Do the same for ARC-Easy and ARC-Challenge using their actual n_opt histograms. Restate which constructs survive; if MMLU-Pro no longer clears, rewrite the abstract sentence, intro bullet 1, Table 1/Table 10 verdict columns and the Reproducibility Statement accordingly. Print the n_opt histogram used, so the null is reproducible. As a sanity assertion in the emitter, add a check that E[f_hat] >= max_L E[m_hat_L] for every row — the current numbers would have failed it.
issues.verification_test: Add to the emitter an assertion that for every row E[f_hat] >= the null expectation of any single legal-letter marginal, and specifically that the MMLU-Pro rows satisfy E[f_hat] >= 0.110877. Then re-emit Table 1/Table 10 and confirm (a) both MMLU-Pro rows now show E[f_hat] in ~0.1134-0.1139 and p in ~0.05-0.10, (b) the abstract's surviving-construct count matches the re-emitted verdict column, and (c) an independent reimplementation of the item-wise-legal null (per-stratum multinomial, 2e5 draws, published n_opt histogram) reproduces the printed E[f_hat]/q95/p to 4 decimals.

issues.location: Section 3.2 (sections/03_method.tex lines 75-79, definition of recovery_fraction and the 0.10x materiality gate) and Section 5.1 (sections/05_analysis.tex line 27, 'assigns recovery_fraction=0.049, only 9.1% of the intact-family anchor'), plus Section 5.3 (line 43, anchor 0.0545)
issues.description: Two problems with the gate statistic. First, it is 0/0 exactly on the class of arm the paper cares most about. recovery_fraction = Delta_perm / Delta_max, where Delta_max is the best alignment achievable by reassigning the observed prediction multiset. The paper proves (correctly) that a pure constant emitter has Delta_perm = 0; but for the same emitter Delta_max - acc_hat = 0 as well, since permuting a constant multiset cannot improve alignment. I verified this numerically on a two-stratum construction: all-A gives Delta_perm = +0.000000 pp and Delta_max - acc_hat = +0.000000 pp, so the gate statistic is undefined, not zero, for literal constant emitters — and the paper elsewhere reports sixteen damaged cross-family cells whose accuracy equals the emitted letter's marginal to machine precision. For the near-constant regime actually reported (Qwen3 k14 emits A on 94.6% of items) the denominator is small and the ratio is a quotient of two near-zero percentage-point quantities, reported as 0.049 with no interval and compared to an anchor 0.0545 also reported with no interval; two point estimates in the third decimal decide a published label ('real but immaterial'). Second, the two numbers are mutually inconsistent as stated: 0.049/0.0545 = 0.899, i.e. 89.9%, not the '9.1%' the text asserts. Either the ratio, the anchor, or the percentage is wrong; if '9.1%' is computed against some other anchor (~0.538) that anchor is not identified anywhere in the text, and the E-D file that would settle it is not shipped (R5-02).
issues.proposed_fix: Resolve the 0.049 / 0.0545 / 9.1% inconsistency explicitly, naming the anchor quantity and its value. Give recovery_fraction a bootstrap interval (it is a ratio of resampled quantities, so this is free given the existing 10,000 paired resamples) and refuse the gate when the interval on Delta_max covers zero. Define the gate's behaviour at Delta_max = 0 explicitly as undefined-and-blocked rather than letting a 0/0 propagate, and say so in the method, mirroring the paper's existing 'anchor blocked' machinery.
issues.verification_test: Recompute recovery_fraction with a 95% bootstrap interval for Qwen3 k14 and the Llama-2 intact anchor and confirm the stated percentage-of-anchor equals ratio_arm/ratio_anchor to the printed precision. Separately, construct a synthetic pure always-L prediction vector on the MMLU-Pro item set, run it through the v2 emitter, and confirm the code returns an explicit undefined/blocked verdict rather than a number.
